channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Policy support tempers KRW losses – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Hardman links a sharp correction in South Korean AI‑heavy equities to potential pressure on the Korean Won.

item.title: Forex Today: Markets assess Japanese GDP as ECB decision looms
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades with a cautious tone near the 100.00 region as investors balance resilient United States (US) economic data against improving global risk sentiment following reports that Iran has ended its military operations against Israel.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Appreciation trend outweighs yield gap – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen notes that despite the People’s Bank of China (PBoC) relaxing the cap on US Dollar (USD) deposit rates, the Chinese Yuan has already appreciated about 3% against the Dollar this year.

item.title: United States Dollar Index eases as Iran halts military operations against Israel
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback's value against a basket of six major currencies, edges lower on Monday as traders assess the evolving situation in the Middle East.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Further losses against US Dollar toward 1.2960 – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that USD/SGD surged past 1.29 after a blowout US nonfarm payrolls report, with the S$NEER still trading well above its mid-point.

item.title: CEE FX: Zloty most vulnerable in risk-off – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky highlights that Central and Eastern European FX is being driven by global headlines and hawkish US repricing, with local data having limited impact.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD hovers near 200-day SMA, downside risks persist
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades modestly higher on Monday after falling nearly 8% on Friday in the wake of a stronger-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report, which reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will keep interest rates higher for longer.

item.title: WTI Oil climbs as Israel-Iran, Houthi tensions eclipse OPEC+ output hike
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $89.95 at the time of writing on Monday, up 1.57% on the day, as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to support energy prices.

item.title: South Korean Won: Authorities step up FX defence – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights that South Korean policymakers held an emergency meeting and vowed stern action against speculative FX activity as USD/KRW trades at its weakest since 2009. The National Pension Service has resumed forward FX selling under a higher hedge ratio framework.

item.title: India: Hawkish RBI stance and FY27 risks – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao says the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept its policy rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance but a clearly hawkish tone, focused on inflation and currency stability.

item.title: NY Fed Consumer Inflation Expectations mostly unchanged in May, job market weakening
item.description: The New York Federal Reserve Bank released its May Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE) on Monday, in which households expect inflation to edge down a tick, despite upward pressures from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average trails chip rebound while CPI lines up to spoil it
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) sat almost unchanged into the European afternoon, futures drifting around the 50,750 area after an overnight session that climbed off a low close to 50,500 up toward the 51,000 line before rolling straight over.

item.title: Canadian Dollar softens as Gulf peace hopes weigh on Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD trades in a narrow range on Monday, with the Canadian Dollar (CAD) struggling to capitalize on a softer US Dollar (USD) as a mild pullback in Crude Oil prices weighs on the commodity-linked Loonie. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.3950, holding near two-month highs.

item.title: British Pound edges higher as Iran-Israel halt hostilities
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) registers modest gains of 0.10% on Monday as risk appetite improves despite attacks exchanged between Iran and Israel, which agreed to halt fire as US President Donald Trump demanded the end of shooting to resume talks between Washington and Tehran.

item.title: Euro elevates as ECB decision takes center stage
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades near 1.1540 on Monday as investors assess mixed Eurozone sentiment data and position ahead of the European Central Bank's (ECB) highly anticipated interest rate decision later this week.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Unemployment focus urged – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada’s (NBC) Warren Lovely, Stéfane Marion and Matthieu Arseneau argue that the Bank of Canada (BoC) should add an explicit unemployment rate forecast to its quarterly Monetary Policy Report.

item.title: Euro area: Growth noise and inflation outlook – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists argue that the negative 1Q Gross Domestic Product (GDP) print mainly reflects Irish volatility rather than broad weakness, with ex‑Ireland growth at 0.3% qoq and stronger PMI and French industrial data.

item.title: Gold holds near its lowest level since March as hawkish Fed outlook caps gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) recovers some ground on Monday after sliding to its lowest level since March, as traders assess fresh geopolitical developments in the Middle East. However, hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations continue to cap the upside.

item.title: Norwegian Krone : Norges Bank stance supports NOK crosses – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad (BBH) notes that May Consumer Price Index (CPI) in Norway could be pivotal, with a hot print potentially bringing forward another Norges Bank hike after its surprise May move.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI measures support INR near term – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan analyses new Reserve Bank of India and government measures that could generate around US$40bn of inflows and partially plug India’s FY2026/27 balance of payments gap.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles to gain traction despite softer US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY holds firm on Monday as traders track rapidly changing headlines from the Middle East. Lingering concerns about another intervention by Japanese authorities also limit the pair's upside as the Japanese Yen (JPY) once again tests the 160.00 level against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: US Dollar: Safe-haven bid with conflict and yields – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage notes that escalating Middle East tensions and higher U.S. Treasury yields are driving risk-off flows, with the Dollar supported at two‑month highs.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy hold as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence expect the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep the overnight rate at 2.25% at the June meeting and through 2026, despite softer Canadian data.

item.title: Euro: ECB hike seen limiting upside versus US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to deliver a one-off 25 bp ‘insurance’ hike to 2.25%, with updated projections showing higher inflation and weaker growth.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Policymakers target FX stability around fair value – ING
item.description: ING economists Peter Virovacz and Zoltán Homolya highlight that the Hungarian Forint (HUF) has sharply appreciated, with investors now treating Hungary as a quasi-eurozone economy.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause outlook after strong US jobs – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Alvin Liew notes that stronger-than-expected US payrolls and higher Oil prices have sharply reduced expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026.

item.title: Australian Dollar advances as RBA stance supports recovery ahead of key US, China data
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7070 at the time of writing on Monday, up 0.33% on the day, after touching a low near 0.7024, its weakest level in nearly two months.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed support and risk backdrop – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the US Dollar (USD) remains firm as United States (US) jobs data, higher Federal Reserve (Fed) rate expectations and rising Oil prices pressure stocks and bonds.

item.title: United Kingdom: BoE stance and Burnham politics – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s United Kingdom (UK) economists highlight political uncertainty around Andy Burnham’s potential Labour leadership challenge and its policy implications, but still expect limited radical change.

item.title: Euro: Mixed macro backdrop with weak Germany – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage flags that Euro area Sentix sentiment remains in downturn territory, with Germany still classified in recession despite modest improvement. German manufacturing orders fell sharply in April, driven by autos and machinery, even as sales showed some resilience.
